text:
maya: heads-up 1 i prototyped a compact client-error surface for API + console badges. want quick ops/ux review before RFC.

devon: sounds good. are we changing status semantics or just adding metadata?

maya: keep semantics: 429=quota, 503=capacity/backpressure, 424=downstream. add three headers: `x-rw-reason`, `x-rw-retryable` (true/false), `x-rw-retry-hint` (secs/text).

sai: single header vs multiple? single blob is compact but breaks our parsers. prefer flat headers.

lex: flat headers win for dashboards. also ensure telemetry emits `client_surface_bucket` tag.

sofia: console badges = OK | THROTTLED | DEGRADED | UNAVAILABLE. copy must be short (<80 chars). examples: "Rate limit reached 1 requests paused. Retry after {n}s or request more quota."

maya: mapping draft:
429 + reason=quota -> THROTTLED, retryable=true, retry-hint=Retry-After or secs
503 + reason=backpressure -> DEGRADED, retryable=false
424 + reason=downstream -> UNAVAILABLE, retryable=false, retry-hint="contact support"
5xx generic -> UNAVAILABLE, retryable=false, retry-hint="try later"

rui: note: exposing retryable must be careful for non-idempotent endpoints. telemetry must record `retryable` so SDKs can opt-in.

devon: agree. SDKs should surface headers behind a feature flag initially.

lex: infra ask: add short-window metric for backpressure to avoid misclassifying capacity as quota.

sofia: UX will provide final one-liners and a/b copy options.

maya: rollout plan: internal canary -> tag telemetry -> 2-week canary -> default. include an S3 reclassification job to migrate historical events for dashboard continuity.

ops-bot: preview deploy: https://deploys.internal/redwood/preview/1987 branch=error-taxonomy-headers

rui: also log both raw headers and resolved badge in traces for runbook clarity.

maya: thanks. i'll update RFC with header names, badge mapping, telemetry tags, migration plan, and canary schedule, then ping for final sign-off.

ops-bot: canary scheduled 2024-11-04T04:00Z (50% traffic).
